mechanism: Tramadol inhibits reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine while melatonin has serotonergic activity, creating additive CNS depression and potential serotonin syndrome risk; both agents also increase sedation through different pathways.
action: Monitor for excessive sedation, serotonin syndrome symptoms (agitation, confusion, tremor, hyperthermia), and counsel patients to avoid concurrent use if possible or use cautiously with dose adjustment and patient education.
